# Independent audit: raw moment John maxima and mass stationarity

Source: `candidate 43892fde2d187dd5`,
including the anchor-deletion addition. **PASS**, with no depth-selector
inference.

## Boundary support uniqueness and strict interpolation

Weak-star compactness applies because the finite source is bounded and
all constrained moments are integrals of L1 functions. Fiberwise upper
cap rearrangement preserves both total mass and integer first moment.
Its strict equality condition holds for every nonzero continuous
direction because all corresponding level sets have zero fiber volume.
Consequently every support-maximizing source is an indicator in each
fiber. Two distinct maximizing sources at the same constraint pair
would have a fractional average on a positive-measure set; rearranging
one such fiber would strictly improve that average while preserving
its constraints. Thus the global support source is unique.

This argument remains valid at saturated or boundary constraint pairs:
it requires no finite ambient cap dual there. At two distinct pairs,
the unique support indicators differ. Their strict mixture is fractional
and therefore strictly suboptimal in every support direction. Continuity
of the fixed compact bodies' support functions and compactness of the
unit sphere turn these pointwise strict gaps into a uniform positive
inball. The strict determinant-root inequality follows by adding that
inball to the Minkowski average of inscribed ellipsoids, including
singular endpoint shapes.

## Attainment, interior masses, and integer averaging

The compact graph bounds the centers and shapes of all inscribed
ellipsoids. Subsequential limits remain inscribed, giving upper
semicontinuity of the John radius and attainment over each compact mass
interval and the finite set of positive-mass feasible integer bases.
Mixing the empty source and any positive single-fiber source proves a
positive achievable radius. Strict concavity gives uniqueness of each
maximizing mass.

At a positive source base `j`, every mass-`T_j` source must fill its
entire own fiber: adding any missing density there preserves balance
about `j` and otherwise contradicts maximality of `T_j`. Therefore an
arbitrary own-fiber source of mass epsilon may be removed from every
maximum-mass source. This proves the full Minkowski inclusion
`Q_(T_j-epsilon)(j) superset Q_(T_j)(j)-Z_epsilon(K_j)`.
It is not merely an assertion about one chosen extremal source.

The homothetic sources used in the note give an explicit positive
inball in `Z_epsilon(K_j)` whenever `0<epsilon<|K_j|`. Addition of its
negative strictly enlarges a positive-radius inscribed ellipsoid; a
zero-radius boundary section is already beaten by an interior one.
Thus every positive-base maximizing mass lies strictly between zero
and its capacity, with all deletion densities respecting the original
upper bound one.

The harmonic mixing coefficients satisfy exactly
`sum alpha_i t_i=t_0` and
`sum alpha_i t_i j_i=t_0 sum rho_i j_i`. A nontrivial integer average
of maximizing bases therefore gives a feasible constraint pair whose
John radius is strictly larger than the common maximum. This excludes
both additional integer points in the hull and nonvertex maximizing
bases. The parity bound follows without assuming equal masses or
interior endpoint sections. For actual compatible fibers, every
integer point in the hull of the positive bases has a positive-volume
Minkowski average in its actual fiber, so all feasible integer bases
are positive source bases and the interior-mass conclusion applies.

## Prescribed-slope cap duals

The one-base joint raw body has full dimension `d+1`, and its sections
are Hausdorff continuous at interior masses. Mixing with the zero
source or a fixed larger-mass source supplies the needed lower
convergence; the compact graph supplies upper convergence. An interior
section center consequently persists at two neighboring masses.

For a supporting plane of prescribed slope `b`, restricting to the
minimal base face is legitimate: every balanced source is supported
on that face. A uniformly fractional balanced source on all its
fibers gives the stated coercive lower bound for the free-mass hinge
as a function of the integer tilt. The seminorm is a norm on the
chosen face span. The hinge therefore attains its minimum; its
derivative imposes base balance because the continuous normal is
nonzero and all zero levels have measure zero. Pointwise hinge
duality then proves optimality among balanced sources of every mass.

The prescribed supporting source has that same optimum. Equality in
the positive-part inequality identifies it with the unique cap source,
so its mass and raw moment are exactly the prescribed ones. A finite
exposing coefficient removes all fibers outside the minimal face
without changing the prescribed slope or any on-face trace. This
establishes actual ambient cap duals with the required slope, not
merely unspecified supporting hyperplanes.

## Augmented John contacts and mass stationarity

At an interior maximizing mass, a joint supporting plane active on
the normalized unit ball has nonzero continuous normal; its normalized
continuous part is the corresponding ball contact direction. Evaluating
the plane at the center in two neighboring masses bounds all slopes.
Thus the augmented contact triples `(-b,v,vv^T)` form a compact set.
Their conic hull is closed because the trace of the last coordinate
bounds the total coefficient in every convergent conic sequence.

If `(0,0,I)` lay outside this cone, separation would provide a mass,
center, and symmetric-shape variation with positive volume derivative
and nonpositive first-order motion at every active support. Subtracting
a small scalar identity from the shape makes these inequalities
uniformly strict while keeping positive trace. Near the compact active
set, the support expansion then has uniform negative first-order sign;
away from it, compactness gives a positive initial support gap. This
proves actual containment of a larger ellipsoid at the varied mass.
The argument also controls nearly vertical full supporting normals:
none is active at the initial interior mass, and the active slopes are
uniformly bounded. Hence the proposed variation contradicts maximality.

Finite conic Caratheodory gives the contact weights with the stated
cardinality, including `sum lambda_i b_i=0`. Returning from normalized
raw coordinates leaves these mass slopes unchanged. The cap support
identities then give exactly `sum lambda_i Psi_i=d`. The averaged cap
source is dominated, and the stated covariance refers explicitly to
its constituent centroids; within-component variance is not discarded.

The integer tilt sum is retained. The two complementary anchor-space
covers follow from the pointwise zero weighted margin, without
asserting coverage or zero tilt at other bases.

## Complementation and boundary cases

Complementing densities gives the exact reflected raw moment body at
the complementary mass and base moment. Strict concavity makes their
common midpoint the unique maximum over all real constraint pairs.
When the true base centroid is integral, this is also the unique
integer optimum, and central symmetry of its raw moment body places
its John center at the raw full-centroid moment. Dividing by the
selected mass yields the original centroid. The `n=0` case is included
with one base and mass `M/2`.

For a binary product, balance at a base vertex confines sources to its
single positive fiber. Single-fiber complementation and strictness give
the unique mass `|K|/2`, and all binary bases have the same John radius.
Thus the parity bound is sharp. None of these geometric identifications
implies that an arbitrary selected center has OC depth.
